csdrg.title: Clinical Study Data Reviewer's Guide (lite): DEMO-301
csdrg.notice: Synthetic data for demonstration. Not from any real study.
csdrg.scope: Generated from one pipeline run. It follows the section order of the PHUSE cSDRG template for the parts a run can state as facts: data flow, standards, datasets, conformance and derivations. Protocol and data collection narratives, and sponsor decisions on unresolved issues, are not generated. This is a demonstration of a deterministic pipeline on synthetic data, not a production submission workflow.

dataFlow.label: Study definition
dataFlow.summary: Reads the USDM study design: arms, epochs, visits, activities.

dataFlow.label: Collected data
dataFlow.summary: Generates seeded synthetic subjects from the USDM schedule.

dataFlow.label: SDTM
dataFlow.summary: Tabulates trial design and subject domains.

dataFlow.label: Conformance
dataFlow.summary: Checks datasets against controlled terminology and rule ids.

dataFlow.label: Define-XML
dataFlow.summary: Generates dataset metadata from the same specifications.

dataFlow.label: Package
dataFlow.summary: Serialises Dataset-JSON, CSV and XPT with a hashed manifest.

conformance.scopeNotice: Models a subset of published SDTMIG 3.4 and ADaMIG 1.3 rules. Run CDISC CORE for the complete published conformance catalog.

issues.message: Actual visit falls outside the TV planned window.
issues.citation: SDTMIG 3.4 / SDTM and SDTMIG Conformance Rules 2.0: https://www.cdisc.org/standards/foundational/sdtmig/sdtm-and-sdtmig-conformance-rules-v2-0
issues.explanation: The generator moves about 7% of scheduled post-baseline visits two days past the end of their planned window, as happens in real studies. SVSTDY is correct: the visit happened late. ADaM assigns these records to analysis visits by the window rule (BDS_WINDOW).

issues.message: Partial adverse-event onset date needs review for temporal analyses.
issues.citation: SDTMIG 3.4 / SDTM and SDTMIG Conformance Rules 2.0: https://www.cdisc.org/standards/foundational/sdtmig/sdtm-and-sdtmig-conformance-rules-v2-0
issues.explanation: About 12% of post-dose adverse events are given a month-only onset date, as a site might record when the day is unknown. AESTDY is left missing in SDTM; ADAE imputes the day and flags it (ADAE_IMPUTE).

issues.message: Adverse event began before first exposure.
issues.citation: SDTMIG 3.4 / SDTM and SDTMIG Conformance Rules 2.0: https://www.cdisc.org/standards/foundational/sdtmig/sdtm-and-sdtmig-conformance-rules-v2-0
issues.explanation: About 7% of randomized subjects have an adverse event two days before first dose. These records stay in AE and are not treatment-emergent in ADAE (ADAE_TEAE).

issues.message: Synthetic laboratory result is outside the reference range.
issues.citation: SDTMIG 3.4 / SDTM and SDTMIG Conformance Rules 2.0: https://www.cdisc.org/standards/foundational/sdtmig/sdtm-and-sdtmig-conformance-rules-v2-0
issues.explanation: About 2.5% of laboratory results are generated at 1.8 times the expected value and flagged LBNRIND = HIGH, so that shift and abnormality summaries have something to count. The values are deliberate, not entry errors.

derivations.text: Start date of the subject's exposure record (EXSTDTC); missing for subjects never dosed.
End date of the subject's exposure record (EXENDTC); missing for subjects never dosed or with no exposure end date.

The latest complete date on any of the subject's collected records: consent, randomization, visits, exposure, concomitant medications, medical history, eligibility, adverse events, vital signs, ECGs, laboratory tests and disposition events. Partial dates are ignored.
Date of the subject's DEATH disposition event (DSSTDTC); missing for subjects with no recorded death.
Y when the subject has a DEATH disposition event; missing otherwise.
Arm code and arm from the subject's randomization record; missing for subjects never randomized, whose reason is in ARMNRS.

The code and name of the planned arm whose treatment the subject received (EXTRT on their exposure record). Missing, with the reason in ARMNRS, for a subject never dosed or dosed with a treatment no arm plans.

Why ARMCD or ACTARMCD is missing, as an Arm Null Reason (C142179) term: SCREEN FAILURE for a subject never randomized or dosed, NOT ASSIGNED for one dosed without being randomized, ASSIGNED, NOT TREATED for one randomized and never dosed, and UNPLANNED TREATMENT for one dosed with a treatment no arm plans. Missing when both arms are known.
The treatment a subject received (EXTRT) when no planned arm names it, so ACTARMCD is missing with ARMNRS = UNPLANNED TREATMENT; missing for every other subject.
Y when the visit is one of the planned visits in TV; missing for an unscheduled visit.
For a planned visit, Y when the visit has a date and N when it was missed; missing for an unscheduled visit.
Days from RFSTDTC (first exposure) to the record date, plus one when the date is on or after RFSTDTC; there is no Day 0. Missing when either date is missing or partial.
Number each subject's records from 1 in the order they are tabulated.
Collected dose unit, which is already the UNIT submission value (TABLET, C48542).

Dose form of the investigational product in the USDM administrable product, written as its Dosage Form (C66726) submission value: TABLET for C42998. Missing when the study names no investigational product or its dose form is not in the codelist.

The epoch on the record date, in USDM epoch order: before first exposure the first epoch, from first through last exposure the second, after that the third, kept only when TA lists it. Records of subjects never dosed are in the first epoch; a missing or partial date gives no epoch, and so does a medication started before informed consent.

Looked up from the reported name (CMTRT) in the study's fictional drug dictionary, which has WHODrug's shape but is not WHODrug: standardized names are generic drug names, class names are plain descriptions and class codes are synthetic, starting with Z, a letter the ATC classification does not use. Missing when the reported name is not in the dictionary.
When the medication was marked ongoing at the end of the subject's participation, CMENRTPT is ONGOING (Relation to Reference Period, C66728) and CMENTPT is END OF STUDY; both are missing otherwise.

Looked up from the preferred term (AEDECOD) in the study's fictional adverse event dictionary, which has MedDRA's five levels but is not MedDRA: its lower and group level names are invented and its codes are synthetic, from 99000000. Each lowest level term is its preferred term. Missing when the preferred term is not in the dictionary.
Collected causality mapped to the submission value: RELATED is written as POSSIBLY RELATED; other values are kept.

Looked up from the reported term (MHTERM) in the study's fictional event dictionary, the one adverse events are coded with, which has MedDRA's shape but is not MedDRA: MHDECOD is the preferred term and MHBODSYS its primary system organ class, and the codes are synthetic, from 99000000. Missing when the reported term is not in the dictionary.
When the condition was marked ongoing at the screening visit, MHENRTPT is ONGOING (Relation to Reference Period, C66728) and MHENTPT is SCREENING; both are missing otherwise.
The criterion text TI holds for the same IETESTCD, so IE and TI cannot disagree; missing when TI has no such criterion.
IE records only the criteria a subject did not meet: N (No Yes Response, C66742) for an INCLUSION criterion and Y for an EXCLUSION criterion. IESTRESC repeats IEORRES.
Test name and standard unit of the USDM biomedical concept for the test code.
The collected numeric result written as text.

The collected result in the test's standard unit, as text in --STRESC and as a number in --STRESN: as collected when the collected unit is the standard unit, otherwise converted by a fixed factor and rounded to two decimals. The one conversion defined is glucose from mg/dL to mmol/L (divide by 18.016); with any other unit the standard result is missing.
Y on the subject's latest record for the test dated on or before first exposure; missing otherwise.
The laboratory panel of the test at the study's fictional central laboratory: CHEMISTRY for ALT, AST, BILI, CREAT and GLUC; HEMATOLOGY for HGB, WBC and PLAT.

Lower and upper limits of the test's reference range at the study's fictional central laboratory, in standard units for --STNRLO and --STNRHI (numbers) and, when the result was collected in the standard unit, in original units for --ORNRLO and --ORNRHI (text). The original-unit limits are missing when the collected unit differs.

Number each subject's AE and CM pairs from 1, in CM order. A pair is a medication whose collected related adverse event number (CMAENO) names one of the subject's tabulated adverse events; both records of the pair share the RELID.

The TA elements of the subject's actual arm (ACTARMCD), one for each epoch the subject entered, with TA's ETCD, ELEMENT, TAETORD and EPOCH. Every subject entered the first epoch at informed consent, a dosed subject the second at first exposure, and the third only when they have a record dated after last exposure. A subject never randomized has only the first element, which every arm shares. A subject dosed with a treatment no arm plans has an unplanned element for the second epoch (ETCD = UNPLAN, with no ELEMENT or TAETORD), and the elements every arm shares for the others.
The date the subject entered the element: informed consent (RFICDTC) for the first epoch's element, first exposure (EXSTDTC) for the second and last exposure (EXENDTC) for the third.
The start of the subject's next element, so that elements leave no gap; for the subject's last element, the end of participation (RFPENDTC).
For an unplanned element (ETCD = UNPLAN), the treatment the subject received in it, as DM.ACTARMUD records it; missing for every planned element.

The record the site attached the comment to, named on the comments form by its collected source ID: RDOMAIN is that record's domain, IDVAR its --SEQ, or VISITNUM for a visit in SV, and IDVARVAL the value. A comment whose record was not tabulated is not written.

conformance.scopeNotice: Models a subset of published SDTMIG 3.4 and ADaMIG 1.3 rules. Run CDISC CORE for the complete published conformance catalog.

derivations.text: Planned treatment comes from DM. Actual treatment and dates come from first and last EX records.
Safety: dosed; ITT: randomized and dosed; efficacy: ITT with baseline and postbaseline systolic blood pressure.
Select the latest nonmissing assessment on or before first dose; a designated baseline visit on first-dose day is eligible.
End-of-study status and discontinuation reason come from the final DS disposition event.
Date of death is DM.DTHDTC when that is a full date; missing for subjects with no recorded death. No death date is imputed.
Assign observed assessments to USDM visit windows; closest target day wins, then earlier date, then lower source sequence.
CHG is AVAL minus BASE; PCHG is 100 times CHG divided by nonzero BASE.
For each subject, parameter and analysis visit, select the observed row closest to target day, then earlier date, then lower source sequence.
For a missing postbaseline visit, carry the latest earlier postbaseline result as a flagged sensitivity row; exclude it from primary ANL01FL selection.
QTcF records only: CRIT1FL is Y when AVAL exceeds 500 ms, and CRIT2FL is Y when CHG exceeds 60 ms, the ICH E14 categorical thresholds for a QTc outlier. CRIT2FL is blank when there is no baseline.
Impute month-only AE starts to the first day, or first dose when it lies in that month; impute month-only ends to month end capped at last contact. Flag imputed days.
A treatment-emergent AE starts from first dose through 14 days after last dose, capped at last known study contact.
Flag the first treatment-emergent occurrence overall, by body system and by preferred term, ordered by analysis start date and AE sequence.

Impute month-only medication starts to the first day, or first dose when it lies in that month; impute month-only ends to month end capped at last contact. Flag imputed days. A medication marked ongoing has no analysis end date.
ASTDY and AENDY count from first dose (ADSL.TRTSDT) as day 1, with no day 0: the analysis date minus TRTSDT, plus 1 on or after first dose. Missing when either date is missing.

For a dosed subject, PREFL is Y when the medication started before first dose, or has no analysis start date. ONTRTFL is Y when it started on or before the end of the on-treatment period (14 days after last dose, capped at last known contact) and ended on or after first dose, or has no analysis end date. A medication started before and continued after first dose has both flags. Both are blank for a subject never dosed.
RESCUEFL is Y when the medication was recorded as rescue medication (CM.CMCAT is RESCUE MEDICATION), and blank otherwise.

TTADISC: an event is the first treatment-emergent AE with drug withdrawal corroborated by an adverse-event DS disposition, dated at the AE start date. TTDTH: death, dated at ADSL.DTHDT. TTSAE: the first serious treatment-emergent AE, dated at its analysis start date. TTRESC: the first rescue medication (ADCM.RESCUEFL = Y) started on or after first dose, dated at its analysis start date. TTSAE and TTRESC count only events up to the end of the on-treatment period.

AVAL counts first-dose day as day 1. TTADISC: a dosed subject without an event is censored at the earlier of last known contact and discontinuation for another reason. TTDTH: censored at last known contact. TTSAE and TTRESC: censored at the end of the on-treatment period, 14 days after last dose, or at last known contact when that is earlier.

One record per ITT subject per component of the hierarchical composite, in priority order (PARAMN): 1 death (ADTTE TTDTH), 2 first serious TEAE (ADTTE TTSAE), 3 first rescue medication (ADTTE TTRESC), 4 change from baseline in systolic blood pressure at Week 12 (ADVS PARAMCD = SYSBP, AVISIT = WEEK 12, ANL01FL = Y). ADT and CNSR are copied from the source record; AVAL is derived as the value-level metadata of each parameter describes.
AVAL and CNSR are the ADTTE values for the same subject and parameter: days from first dose, with CNSR = 1 when the subject was censored.
ANL01FL is Y when AVAL is not missing. A component with a missing AVAL is a tie for every pair that reaches it.
